newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt meets party leaders on economic plan.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt meets party leaders on economic plan.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi met parliamentary party leaders allied to the government on Thursday to discuss a three-year economic strategy which the cabinet is due to approve on Friday.
Prodi was accompanied by Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco and Labour Minister Tiziano Treu during the hour-long meeting.
The meeting was also attended by the parliamentary party leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation, on whose support the government relies to secure a majority in the lower house of parliament.
The government will meet trade union leaders and employers at 1500 gmt when it will spell out details of the economic strategy, known as the DPEF.
Trade unions and Communist Refoundation say they are opposed to any roll-back of the welfare state. The government says Italy's pensions bill is growing at unsustainable rate.
